section_summary: This section covers Japanese civil and military aviation, airline expansion, airfields, subsidies, and restrictions on foreign operators in the 1930s. A substantial 1930 correspondence file follows Ford Motor Company’s effort to demonstrate an aircraft in Japan and China, documenting permits, flight restrictions, and objections to Japanese control over flights across the South Manchuria Railway zone. The section also contains file notes, routing slips, aviation research correspondence, and material filed by cross-reference.

subfiles.title: Civil and naval aviation strength
subfiles.about: Compares civil pilot and aircraft numbers and assesses Japanese naval aviation growth.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that Japan’s weak civil aviation concerns its armed services, which see civilian flying as a military reserve. It contrasts press figures for naval aircraft and squadrons with a naval attaché’s higher estimates.

subfiles.title: File note on foreign airlines in Japan
subfiles.about: Cross-references a despatch stating that no foreign air transport lines operate in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew’s despatch on foreign air transport in Japan.

subfiles.title: Establishment of Air Transport Lines
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese policy and law governing foreign and domestic air transport.
subfiles.summary: Grew states that no foreign or American air transport lines operate in Japan and that foreign aircraft need discretionary permission for paid domestic carriage. He describes Japanese lines, airfield development, and a 1934–35 subsidy of ¥1,429,837. Although the law allows exceptions and Japan has ratified the Paris air navigation convention, he expects foreign applications to be refused on safety and military grounds.

subfiles.summary: Charge slip for file 894.796/35.

subfiles.summary: Requests review of the commercial aviation section on page four.

subfiles.title: Japanese aviation report No. 7722
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese air accidents, maneuvers, civil aviation, airfields, routes, aircraft research, and gliding.
subfiles.summary: The report lists recent military air accidents and exercises, pilot training, and donations of aircraft. It discusses a proposed ¥250 million civil aviation program, disputes within the Japan Aviation Club, and new or proposed fields and services across Japan and its overseas routes. It also covers aircraft research, glider certification, and airport improvements. William H. Crane approves the report.

subfiles.summary: Notes visas for two Japanese aircraft engineers investigating aircraft design and manufacture.

subfiles.title: File note on proposed Japanese air routes
subfiles.about: Cross-references proposed lines linking Japan with Formosa, Sakhalin, Korea, and China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew’s despatch on proposed Japanese air routes.

subfiles.title: Aviation excerpt on new air routes
subfiles.about: Reports planned railway ministry appropriations for overseas air routes.
subfiles.summary: A press report says the 1936–37 budget may fund routes to Formosa, Sakhalin, Korea, and China.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese airline plans
subfiles.about: Cross-references proposed service to the Netherlands East Indies and a Hong Kong stop.
subfiles.summary: Notes Japanese requests and plans for routes through Taiwan, the Philippines, and Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: File note on Europe–East Asia air service
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report of a proposed Japanese service through Baghdad and Basra.
subfiles.summary: Notes a press claim about a future Japanese airline via Iraq.

subfiles.title: Press excerpt on Japanese and German flights
subfiles.about: Reports an uncorroborated Japanese airline proposal and a Lufthansa survey flight.
subfiles.summary: A clipping claims a Japanese airline will serve Europe via Baghdad and Basra; the commentator doubts it.

subfiles.title: Material for a Study of Aviation in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests statistics and publications for a comparative study of Japanese aviation.
subfiles.summary: Boyce seeks government figures on aircraft manufacture, routes, traffic, pilots, trade, and American exports to Japan, plus recommendations for recent aviation reference books.

subfiles.title: Aviation publications sent to Yokohama
subfiles.from: William P. Wright, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: George S. Messersmith, Department of State
subfiles.about: Lists aviation publications supplied in response to Boyce’s request.
subfiles.summary: Wright encloses U.S. aviation regulations, bulletins, maps, and international news items, and recommends an aircraft yearbook and trade periodicals.

subfiles.summary: Charge slip for file 894.796/45.

subfiles.about: Cross-references a new Japan–China service and airline consolidation.
subfiles.summary: Notes the October service launch and formation of Dai Nippon Air Line Company.

subfiles.title: Japan–China aviation and economic control excerpts
subfiles.about: Describes a new Japan–China air service, airline merger, and related economic reorganization.
subfiles.summary: Japan Air Transport began scheduled flights in October using Douglas and Lockheed aircraft, then merged with International Air Line Company to form Dai Nippon Air Line Company. The following excerpt discusses implementation of economic mobilization measures and proposed policy companies for occupied China.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning a proposed loan to Japan
subfiles.about: Objects to reports of an American loan that might help Japan.
subfiles.summary: Imatovitch urges the president to prevent a reported loan to Japan, arguing that the funds could support purchases while Americans need help.

subfiles.title: Reply to Rachel Imatovitch
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Department of State
subfiles.about: Responds to concerns about American loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton says the Department knows of no such loans or credits apart from ordinary trade credit.

subfiles.title: Ford aircraft shipment file jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the Ford aircraft shipment case.
subfiles.summary: Jacket for the Ford Motor Company aircraft shipment file.

subfiles.title: Conversation with C. I. Poore on Ford aircraft
subfiles.from: W. R. Peck, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Explains export, import, and flight-permit requirements for a Ford demonstration aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Poore describes Ford’s plan to ship an aircraft to Japan and fly it through Manchuria into China. Peck explains that a nonmilitary aircraft needs no U.S. export permit, while Japanese and Chinese authorities require advance flying permission. He identifies the relevant regulations, suggested consular contacts, and documents required for aircraft and crew.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Japanese and Chinese aviation rules
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Department of State
subfiles.to: C. I. Poore, Ford Motor Company
subfiles.about: Sends rules on American aircraft use in Japan and China.
subfiles.summary: Encloses translated Japanese and Chinese rules for Ford’s planned flights.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary’s handwritten note
subfiles.about: Contains an unclear handwritten instruction concerning the Ford aircraft file.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten departmental note; the OCR does not establish its instruction.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note
subfiles.about: Approves a telegram and plans a follow-up letter to Ford.
subfiles.summary: The division will draft a further letter after the telegram is sent.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs routing note
subfiles.about: Assigns a reply to Ford’s January letter after telegrams are sent.
subfiles.summary: Requests a reply to Ford after the telegram goes out.

subfiles.title: Ford request for advance flight authorizations
subfiles.about: Requests diplomatic help obtaining permits for a demonstration tour through Japan and China.
subfiles.summary: Ford gives the aircraft’s shipment date, crew, certificate application, and planned route, and offers to pay cable expenses.

subfiles.title: Ford aircraft certification details
subfiles.about: Records the Ford aircraft’s flight test, registration, and crew licenses.
subfiles.summary: Lists airworthiness certificate 5-AT-C-65, registration NC 406 H, and pilot and mechanic license numbers.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting Chinese flight permission
subfiles.about: Requests advance Chinese permission for Ford’s demonstration itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Provides aircraft, pilot, mechanic, and route details and asks the Legation to obtain and forward required permissions.

subfiles.title: Notice to Ford of permit requests
subfiles.about: Reports that U.S. representatives were instructed to seek Japanese and Chinese flying permissions.
subfiles.summary: Ford is told that permits, if granted, will be mailed to Hutton through the Yokohama consulate.

subfiles.title: Tokyo acknowledgment of Ford telegram
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the Department’s Ford flight telegram.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo confirms receiving a copy of the February 5 telegram.

subfiles.title: Peiping report on permit request
subfiles.about: Reports that China has not yet answered the Ford flight request.
subfiles.summary: The Legation sent a telegram and will follow it with a note.

subfiles.title: Chinese approval for Ford flight
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese permission for Ford’s aircraft to enter China.
subfiles.summary: China permits the flight provided the aircraft carries no contraband and avoids prohibited areas.

subfiles.title: Copy of Chinese flight approval
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Chinese approval and records cable charges.
subfiles.summary: Copy of conditional Chinese approval; notes a $13.91 telegram charge.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Chinese flight approval
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Chinese approval for Ford’s aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of conditional Chinese approval and telegram charge.

subfiles.title: Obstacles to Ford demonstration flights in Japan
subfiles.about: Details delays and restrictive conditions attached to Ford’s Japanese flight permission.
subfiles.summary: Castle says Japanese officials approved the flights only under conditions difficult to meet, including advance notice of routes and timing. Customs held the aircraft until March 26 while demanding written proof of permission. He encloses five exchanged notes and suggests warning future American applicants.

subfiles.title: Embassy request for Ford flight permission
subfiles.about: Requests a general permit for James H. Baer’s Ford aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Seeks Japanese demonstration and onward-flight permission, supplying aircraft and crew credentials.

subfiles.title: Embassy’s proposed demonstration routes
subfiles.about: Specifies proposed Japanese demonstration flights from Tachikawa.
subfiles.summary: Requests flights around Fuji, to Osaka, Sendai, and Fukuoka, and over Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Embassy’s additional documents and transfer flight request
subfiles.about: Provides aircraft and crew certificates and requests a Yokohama–Tachikawa transfer flight.
subfiles.summary: Encloses certificate copies and seeks permission to fly the assembled aircraft from Idemachi to Tachikawa.

subfiles.title: Ford aircraft certificate of airworthiness
subfiles.from: Clarence M. Young, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Certifies a Ford 5-AT-C monoplane as airworthy for export.
subfiles.summary: Certifies export airworthiness for serial number 65 at a 13,500-pound gross weight.

subfiles.title: Ford aircraft operating placard
subfiles.about: States approved weight and loading limits for the Ford aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Sets the aircraft’s gross-weight limit and loading calculations, including crew and passenger limits.

subfiles.title: Japanese conditional approval of Ford flights
subfiles.about: Approves specific Ford routes subject to extensive operational restrictions.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese note prescribes routes and landing fields for demonstration flights and travel toward Mukden and Peiping. It requires advance notice, allows military authorities to change or cancel use of fields, and restricts overflight of Tokyo, fortified zones, and naval areas. Cameras and paid passenger or freight carriage are prohibited.

subfiles.title: Approval of Idemachi–Tachikawa flight
subfiles.about: Allows the Ford aircraft to fly directly from its Yokohama assembly site to Tachikawa.
subfiles.summary: Approves a straight-line route, subject to the earlier note’s conditions.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Ford flight despatch
subfiles.about: Sends the Tokyo despatch and enclosures on obstacles to American demonstration flights.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Castle’s report for use in answering American aviation companies.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of Ford flight report
subfiles.from: Clarence M. Young, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Japanese flight-permit information.
subfiles.summary: Young will consider the report when answering American companies’ inquiries.

subfiles.title: Japanese requirements for flights over South Manchuria Railway zone
subfiles.about: Questions Japan’s demand for permission to cross the South Manchuria Railway zone.
subfiles.summary: The consulate reports that Ford pilot Hutton had to obtain Japanese permission to cross the railway zone, though other foreign aviators apparently had not. It argues that the zone remains Chinese territory and that American flight rights there derive from U.S.–Chinese treaties. The writer sees the new requirement as an unjustified extension of Japanese authority.
